title: Sudden cardiac death risk prediction
bottleneck: Sudden cardiac death kills hundreds of thousands yearly, often as the first manifestation of heart disease; ejection fraction, the main criterion for defibrillator implantation, misses most victims, who have preserved function, while many implanted devices never fire.
why_it_blocks: Prevention depends on identifying at-risk individuals before the event; current risk stratification is too crude in both directions.
current_state: Genetic testing, advanced imaging of scar, and AI-ECG models are improving prediction. Precise, actionable risk stratification for the general population remains out of reach. Most sudden cardiac deaths occur in people never identified as high-risk, limiting the reach of device therapy. Wearable monitoring and AI analysis of routine ECGs offer new avenues for population screening, but false positives and intervention thresholds remain challenging.
